newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil prices seen down in near term.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil prices seen down in near term.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil prices are expected to slip in the next trading week mainly on increased cotton seed supplies, dealers said on Saturday.

"Vegoil prices will fall as we have very good cottonseed production this year which is expected to be over 0.5 million tonnes," dealer Saulat Khan said. "Local production of sunflower and soybean has also been good, which will depress vegoil prices here and lower our vegoil purchases abroad."
Vegoil stocks rose to 168,500 tonnes last week from 160,000 tonnes the previous week after arrivals of fresh supplies.
Dealers said RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks rose to 131,000 tonnes from 125,000 last week. Soybean oil and sunflower oil stocks fell to 24,000 tonnes from 27,000.
The state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan (GCP), which imports vegoil, has stocks of 13,500 tonnes of palm oil and palm olien stocks compared to 8,000 tonnes last week.
The GCP has arranged imports of 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil by October 10. One dealer said a ship was currently discharging 11,660 tonnes of palmoil at Karachi port.

He said one ship with 10,800 tonnes of soyoil was expected to arrive at Karachi on September 20, another with 20,000 tonnes of palmoil on September 18, and a third with about 20,000 on September 19. A vessel is also due to load 20,000 tonnes of palm oil for Pakistan at a Malaysian port in September.
